prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one production TRANSPARENT ROADSIDE PROP SPRITE ATLAS for the original HD-2D road adventure EASTWARD.
Use the attached environment only as a style reference: East Asian industrial highways on an Earth occupied by aliens for ten years; atmospheric realistic volume and materials, subtle pixel-art clusters when seen close, weathered old paint, warm upper-left light and cool gray-teal right-facing shadow. The props should have dimensional form, a visible roof/top plane and visible right-hand side, viewed from a camera slightly above them, nearly side-on for a 2D side-scrolling game. Original understated atmospheric science-fiction, not cartoon vector graphics, not thick black outlined flat icons. No extreme isometric angle.
Generate a square PNG, preferably 1536×1536, laid out as EXACTLY 4 equal columns by 4 equal rows. Sixteen complete, separate props, one per cell, centered with generous transparent gutters (at least 12% margin), no cropping and no intersection between cells. Every ground-contact point near 85% of its own cell height. Transparent background with real alpha. No scenery, ground, shadows on the ground, people, vehicles, logos, readable letters, row numbers or grid lines. Internal self-shadow and material shading are welcome, but no cast ground shadows as those will be dynamic in the game. Restrained amber and muted teal indicator lights; no bright neon glow clouds.
Strict row-major positions, these are eight types each with two visibly different silhouettes:
Row 1:
1. TALL UTILITY POLE A: tapered old concrete electricity pole, two asymmetrical crossbars with ceramic insulators, a transformer can and secured cable loops, scuffed pale markings, short wire ends stay inside the cell.
2. UTILITY POLE B: angular steel A-frame railway-style utility pole with braced crossbeam, junction boxes and subtly grafted alien inspection module, rust and sage paint, different silhouette from single concrete pole.
3. ROAD SIGN A: wide weathered faded-teal rectangular road direction sign on two narrow posts; small cream arrow-like symbols but no readable text, old patches and dents, clearly visible sign thickness and right edge.
4. ROAD SIGN B: three uneven arrow-shaped route plates stacked on one central post, chipped ochre and muted teal paint, a small square amber alien permit marker, visibly different from wide two-post sign.
Row 2:
5. STREETLAMP A: tall bent steel streetlamp with one curved arm and shallow rectangular lamp hood, worn galvanized metal, a dim warm amber fixture, modest junction box near base.
6. STREETLAMP B: tall angular double-arm industrial light pole with two asymmetrical heads and a small muted-teal occupation sensor, worn dark steel, clearly different crown shape.
7. BUS SHELTER A: wide open East Asian concrete bus-stop shelter with sloped corrugated metal roof, two pillars, old wooden bench and glazed back panel, peeling pale teal paint, roof and right wall visible.
8. BUS SHELTER B: compact narrow roadside waiting kiosk with deep flat roof, one enclosed glass side, a small faded route panel and a squat service cabinet, weathered cream and rust paint, no readable text.
Row 3:
9. GUARDRAIL A: low long straight galvanized W-beam roadside guardrail on four posts, bolt detail, upper surface catches warm light, subtle scuffs and a tiny amber reflector.
10. GUARDRAIL B: shorter damaged steel guardrail bent at the center with three braced concrete supports, raised torn end, realistic cool metal highlights, distinct silhouette.
11. ROAD BARRIER A: low heavy Jersey concrete barrier with chipped faded ochre diagonal hazard stripes, inset handles and two tiny amber reflectors, bevelled top and right face visible.
12. ROAD BARRIER B: folding steel checkpoint barricade, long striped horizontal beam over two splayed feet, a squat gray control cabinet at one end with a restrained teal inspection light, old paint and worn corners.
Row 4:
13. FREIGHT CONTAINER A: single long faded sage-green corrugated shipping container with closed right-end doors, clear visible roof and right end, realistic corner castings, small amber occupation seal with abstract symbol but no text.
14. FREIGHT CONTAINER B: weathered rust-red short freight container with one partially open dark door, patched cream panel and roof-mounted narrow equipment box, visibly different silhouette from green closed container.
15. WATER TOWER A: tall cylindrical rust-streaked blue-gray water tank on four slender cross-braced steel legs, small ladder and pipe, visible tank roof rim, subtle warm metal edges.
16. WATER TOWER B: squat square concrete rooftop reservoir on a heavy four-leg metal gantry, external ladder and curved water pipes, a discreet alien meter bolted on one side, different silhouette from cylindrical water tower.
All 16 complete objects must be individually readable at small game size. Do not repeat one design. Scale tall poles and towers to comfortably fit inside their cell; scale wide structures to leave transparent side margins. Nothing may touch another cell.
